back: The change in total cost when one more unit is produced: ΔTC ÷ ΔQ.
Produce where MR = MC: every unit with MR > MC adds to profit; any unit with MR < MC reduces it.
The minimum profit needed to keep the entrepreneur in the industry; counted as a cost (AR = ATC).
Profit above normal profit: AR > ATC; total = (AR − ATC) × output.
AR = AC (TR = TC): the firm earns normal profit only.
Producing at the lowest possible average total cost.
Producing where price = marginal cost, so resources match what consumers value.

front: Why might a loss-making firm keep producing in the short run?
back: If AR covers AVC it pays something towards fixed costs, which must be paid even if it closes.
Where entry is free, abnormal profit attracts new firms; supply rises and price falls until only normal profit remains.
